messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up: noticed a perf regression on dedicated pools when CUDA graphs + KV prefetch are enabled. All-reduce queueing spikes and tail latencies jump ~3x on multi-GPU runs.

Ravi Singh: repro script?

Maya Patel: yep, ran transformer_serving_e2e with batch=8, tp=2 pp=1, kv_warmup=true, graph_mode=on. attaching timeline snippet:

Sara Lopez: can you paste the nvtx timeline / brief logs?

Maya Patel: paste:
```text
TIMELINE GPU0: [0.0ms] cudaGraphLaunch
[0.6ms] forward_kernel_A
[1.2ms] kv_prefetch (stream2)
[1.6ms] NCCL_AllReduce queued (stream0) -> waits 4.8ms
[6.4ms] allreduce runs
```

Maya Patel: NVTX shows NCCL allreduce queued behind device-to-device memcpy caused by KV prefetch on separate stream; but with graph capture those memcpy ops got captured into the graph and replay timing changed -> no overlap.

Ravi Singh: hmm that's the handshake misalignment we've seen before. cudaGraphCapture serializes stream ordering w.r.t captured kernels. Could be the capture time ordering differs from runtime ordering when KV cache warmup issues reorder memcpys.

Dmitri Ivanov: quick test idea: flip prefetch to use the same stream as compute (fallback) -> does overlap improve? Also try explicit stream::synchronize before graph launch to force ordering.

Sara Lopez: tried same-stream prefetch earlier; it eliminates the queueing but regresses latency for short sequences because prefetch blocks compute. tradeoff.

Maya Patel: perf numbers: graph+separate-stream: p95 72ms; graph+same-stream: p95 58ms; graph+separate-stream w/explicit sync: p95 90ms (worse). baseline no-graph separate-stream: p95 30ms.

Ravi Singh: baseline no-graph is best because runtime batching+dynamic kernel selection allowed better overlapping. We need graph-mode kernel selection fallback that avoids capturing memcpy ordering that blocks NCCL.

Dmitri Ivanov: agree. implement heuristic: if kv_prefetch_size > threshold and using cudaGraphs, force prefetch into dedicated pinned host buffer + cudaMemcpyAsync on compute stream during replay, or patch graph to insert dummy kernel to bump stream ordering.

Sara Lopez: or simpler: when building graph, record dependency edges for NCCL ops so they can be launched on higher priority stream using streamWaitEvent instead of relying on captured implicit ordering.

Maya Patel: can we try a quick patch? I'll canary a branch that: 1) adds "graph_friendly_prefetch" toggle 2) if enabled, prefetch uses memory pinned buf + deferred memcpy in compute stream 3) fall back to runtime path if graph fails.

PerfBot: alert: perf-regression-detect detected 2.9x p95 increase for dedicated-prod pool-3 between deploys 2026-02-12 and 2026-02-13.

Ravi Singh: timestamped profiles attached in the PR. @Sara can you run microbench with nvprof + nccl sockets? I think we need a kernel selection tweak too: prefer smaller kernel variants when graph_mode=on for better latency packing.

Sara Lopez: will run. timeline and flamecharts on the branch by EOD.

Maya Patel: thanks. tagging @eng-runtime-owners. I'll open a canary with flag off by default.

Dmitri Ivanov: note for postmortem: document that CUDA graphs can change implicit stream ordering with captured host->device transfers; kv cache warmup is particularly sensitive. add to runtime docs.

Maya Patel: agreed. short action items:
- Maya: PR for graph_friendly_prefetch (canary)
- Sara: microbench + nvprof traces
- Ravi: kernel selection experiment
- Dmitri: doc note + fallback design

Ravi Singh: ack :thumbsup:

Sara Lopez: ack

PerfBot: deploy-bot: canary started for branch/graph_prefetch_fix on pool-3

Maya Patel: I'll follow up with perf numbers in this thread.
